scenes.prompt: Commissioned editorial photography for T Magazine (New York Times Style), design-object feature; NOT a product render, NOT advertising, NOT stock. Aesthetic reference: Christopher Sturman and Sean Davidson studio still-lifes. Captured on a Hasselblad H6D-100c with a Hasselblad HC 80mm f/2.8 lens at f/5.0 at low 3/4 angle 25 degrees above the surface, framed tight at roughly 28 percent of the frame. The bolo tie lies in one relaxed loose coil on a slab of unsealed travertine, slide face up at the right-third intersection of a 1:1 frame, both metal tips fanned slightly apart, generous gallery negative space at the upper-left. Single soft directional north-window daylight from camera-upper-left, committed to one exposure. Style — only the merest edge of a folded raw oat-cream linen napkin at the bottom-right frame edge, nothing else. CONCRETE IMPERFECTIONS REQUIRED: the travertine slab shows real fossil voids and one filled vein running diagonally with a faint colour shift; one corner of the slab is gently chipped; the raw linen edge has one pulled thread loop and a soft natural crease; one metal aglet shows a 1-2mm scratch and faint thumb-tarnish on its bezel; the braided leather cord shows one knot-crease where it has been worn before; a near-invisible fingerprint smudge sits on the cabochon. REJECT CINEMATIC AI BALANCE: the upper-left of the slab is brighter than the lower-right; let the brightest specular on the slide bezel clip slightly; the lower-right corner falls to genuine committed shadow, not lifted to grey. ZERO COLOR CAST: cool 5500K daylight stays neutral on the travertine; warm leather reads warm, cool stone reads cool, no global wash. PHOTOGRAPHIC TEXTURE: visible Kodak Portra 400 grain in the travertine mid-tones (organic, fine), 1-2 percent corner vignette, pronounced f/5.0 falloff so the linen edge softens into bokeh, 1-2 px purple-cyan chromatic aberration only on the brightest bezel specular. The bolo tie matches the variant reference image exactly — stone colour, hardware finish, and cord colour as shown. Palette of warm travertine cream and amber vein, oat-cream linen, soft metal finish, warm cord leather. No people, no alcohol.

The valet tray and other props echo the bolo's metal finish and cord tone (color-echo rule — brass-toned objects with brown cord, antique-silver objects with black cord).
